title: Bad root-finder output
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube. An optional root decision is declared bad as follows: absence of a decision is not bad, and a constant-sign decision is not bad; a decision to split on a coordinate is bad exactly when that coordinate has zero influence on $f$, where influence is the mean squared discrete derivative under the uniform sign-cube distribution.
hypotheses_covered: Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
optional decision at the root: absent, constant sign, or a coordinate split
